content.text:
Synced groups with different external ids can now share a name, and syncing the same set twice updates the existing groups in place and creates nothing. Type-check is clean, lint shows no problems in the four files I touched, and the 70 tests in the group model, group syncer and groups API test files all pass. I didn't run the full `yarn test` suite.

**What I changed**
- **Name check** (`server/models/Group.ts`): the "name already in use" check now only compares groups with the same `externalId`, still matching names case-insensitively within the team. In practice:
  - Two hand-made groups (no `externalId`) with the same name still conflict.
  - Two groups with the same `externalId` and the same name still conflict.
  - Groups with different external ids can share a name.
- **Group sync** (`server/commands/groupsSyncer.ts`): the sync wasn't storing the provider's id on the groups it created, so every synced group looked hand-made. It now saves the id when it creates a group. It also fills the id in on groups an earlier sync created without one, so teams already stuck on the "already in use" error recover on their next sync.

**Behaviour you might not expect:** a hand-made group and a synced group can have the same name. Hand-made groups are now checked only against other hand-made groups. Otherwise, editing an existing hand-made group would start failing once a synced group with the same name appeared.

**Tests added**
- `server/models/Group.test.ts`: covers each of the name rules above.
- `server/commands/groupsSyncer.test.ts`:
  - Syncs three groups whose names differ only in case, twice; the second sync creates nothing and the group ids don't change.
  - A synced group can share a name with a hand-made one.
  - Groups from an earlier sync with no stored id get it filled in.

Without the fix, 5 of the new tests fail; with it, they all pass.
